questions.question: Materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them are called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulator**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulators: **
 
• Insulators are materials that do not allow the flow of electric current.
 
• **The electrons** in insulator materials are tightly bound to their atoms and do not move freely, thus preventing the flow of electric current.
 
• Examples of insulators include **rubber, glass, and most plastics.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conductors: **

 
 
• Conductors are materials that allow the flow of electric current.
 
• They have free electrons that can move easily between atoms.
 
• This movement of electrons is what we refer to as an electric current.
 
• Examples of good conductors include metals like copper, aluminum, and gold.
 
 
 
• **Capacitors:**
 
 
• Capacitors are not a type of material, but a type of component used in electronic circuits.
 
• A capacitor is a device that stores electrical energy in an electric field.
 
• It is made of two conductive plates separated by an insulator (also called a dielectric).
 
• When a voltage is applied across the plates, an electric field is created and energy is stored.
 
 
 
• **Inductors:**
 
 
• Like capacitors, inductors are also components used in electronic circuits, not a type of material.
 
• An inductor is a coil of wire that stores energy in a magnetic field when electric current flows through it.
 
• The property of an inductor to oppose a change in current is known as inductance.
 
• Inductors are often used in analog circuits and signal processing.

questions.question: Which law explains about the tides due to the moon and the sun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of gravitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The gravitational attraction between two bodies **is directly proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of their distance, according to **Newton's law of universal gravitation.**
 
• As a result, the gravitational attraction between two things increases as their mass increases and their distance decreases.
 
• The main force that causes tides is gravity.** Sir Isaac Newton** explained in 1687 that ocean tides are caused by the sun and moon's gravitational force on the earth's oceans.
 
• The gravitational attractive force is what causes tidal forces. The distance between two objects is frequently more important than their masses when it comes to tidal pressures on Earth.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The angle of the reflected** ray is equal to the angle of the incident ray when reflected off a smooth surface with respect to the normal to the surface, which is a line perpendicular to the surface at the point of contact, according to **the law of reflection**.
 
• **Law of refraction: **At the point of incidence, the incident ray refracted ray, and normal to the interface of two media all lie on the same plane.
 
• **The law of inertia, **commonly known as Newton's first law, states that if a body is at rest or moving in a straight line at a constant speed, it will remain at rest or continue to move in a straight path at constant speed until it is acted with by a force.

questions.question: The materials, through which things can be seen, are called _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transparent materials.**__​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transparent Materials:-**

 
 
• **The materials, through which things can be seen, are called transparent materials.**
 
• Transparent materials allow light to pass through them completely without scattering it. This is why we can see objects clearly through them.
 
• Some examples of transparent materials are:
 
 
• Glass
 
• Water
 
• Air
 
• Clear plastic
 
• Diamonds
 
 
 
• **Transparent materials are used in a variety of applications, such as eyeglasses, windows, lenses, and telescopes.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Opaque materials:-**

 
 
• The materials are those that do not allow light to pass through them. When light strikes an opaque material, it is either absorbed or reflected. This is why we cannot see through opaque materials.
 
 
 
• **Translucent materials:-**
 
 
• These are those that allow light to pass through them, but scatter it in a way that objects behind the material are not clearly visible.
 
• This creates a unique visual effect that can be used in a wide variety of applications, from architecture to fashion.
 
 
 
• **Conductive materials:-**
 
 
• These are those that allow electricity to flow through them. This is because they have a large number of free electrons that can move around and carry the electric current.

questions.question: As per Thermodynamics, ______ system cannot exchange both energy and mass with its surroundings.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**isolated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Isolated system:

__
 
• In an Isolated system, there is no mass and energy interaction across the system boundary i.e. Interaction between the system and the surroundings is absent. Therefore, the mass and the energy of the isolated system are fixed e.g. Universe.
 
• When a body of material starts from a non-equilibrium state of inhomogeneity or chemical non-equilibrium and is then isolated, it spontaneously evolves towards its own internal state of thermodynamic equilibrium.
 
• It is not necessary that all aspects of internal thermodynamic equilibrium be reached simultaneously; some can be established before others. For example, in many cases of such evolution, internal mechanical equilibrium is established much more rapidly than the other aspects of the eventual thermodynamic equilibrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

In thermodynamics, we can classify the system into three types. They are as follows:

Closed System:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52a10999c95170b88a31ceb5cdc9e6ffe68b93c4ec57535658c9ea61139ad950.png] 

 
• There is no mass transfer across the system boundary, but energy transfer takes place in or out of the system.
 
• The contents of a pressure cooker on a stove with its lid tightly closed and the whistle in position is a closed system as no mass can enter or leave the pressure cooker, but heat can be transferred to it. 
 
• A bomb calorimeter only allows heat to be exchanged. Such a system is called closed.

Open System:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d8127767d9a5e448333b116007dd18c9103c736c1c003c9defb565a3cb219f8.png] 

 
• In this type of system, both mass and energy, transfer takes place across the boundary of the system. Examples include pumps, compressors, reactors, distillation columns, heat exchangers, etc.
 
• A centrifugal pump is an open system.

questions.question: Which device is used to either break electric circuit or to complete it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __Switch__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **switch** is a simple device that is used to either break the electric circuit or complete it.
 
• A resistor is a passive electrical component that resists the flow of electric current.
 
• A transistor is a semiconductor device that acts as both an amplifier and a switch.
 
• A fuse is an electrical device for safety that removes electrical current from the circuit if the current gets too high.

questions.question: A ____ is an instrument used for measuring electrical potential difference between two points in an electric circuit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**voltmeter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Voltmeter is an instrument used to measure the potential difference in a circuit.
 
• A voltmeter is always connected in parallel in the circuit to measure the potential difference between two points.
 
• Unit of Potential Difference - Volt.
 
• A galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter by connecting a large resistance in series.
 
• Voltmeter was invented by Hans Orested.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 __Name of the Instrument__
 __Functions/ Used for__
 
 

 **Barometer**
 Measuring atmospheric pressure.
 
 

 **Galvanometer**
 Measuring small electric current.
 
 

 **Ammeter**
 Measuring the strength of the electric current.
 
 

 Pyrometer
 Measuring very high temperature.
 
 

 Calorimeter
 Measuring quantities of heat.
 
 

 Polygraph
 Recording changes, simultaneously in physiological processes such as heartbeat, blood pressure, and respiration is also used as a lie detector.
 
 

 Electrocardiograph (ECG)
 Measuring movements of the heart.
 
 

 Dynamo
 Converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
 
 

 Periscope
 Used for viewing objects above sea level.
 
 

 Electroencephalograph (EEG)
 Measures electrical activities in the brain.
